summary: Admit large host allocations against physical, commit and cgroup headroom the OS reports, not only a logical budget
implementation_scope: Python read-only observations of physical available memory, enforced commit headroom and the tightest ancestor cgroup headroom against min(memory.max, memory.high) (clean page cache only as reclaimable, never shmem), plus admission of a request and reserve against the tightest known observation. Python admit_working_set also distinguishes incremental anonymous, pinned and clean file-backed bytes, checking each applicable domain and defaulting to required physical observation. Native engines use Core's observe_host_memory and admit_host (crit/host_memory.h), which implement the same rules. Reserve policy and denial handling are engine supplied.

agent_guidance.use_when: Large host allocations (pinned staging, resident weights, CPU KV) may share the host with other workloads or run inside a container
agent_guidance.avoid_when: The engine owns a dedicated machine with fixed measured headroom, or allocations are small relative to free memory
provides: Linux MemAvailable and Windows available physical memory
Commit headroom where enforced: Windows always, Linux only with vm.overcommit_memory = 2
Tightest cgroup v2/v1 ancestor headroom against min(memory.max, memory.high), counting only clean page cache (file LRUs, else file - shmem, minus dirty and writeback) as reclaimable
Admission of request plus reserve against the tightest known observation, naming it
Unknown observations reported with reasons and denied by default
Python working-set admission: RAM/cgroup charges all incremental extents, enforced commit charges anonymous plus pinned (Core's admit_host rule)
Guidance for native admission through Core's observe_host_memory and admit_host
engine_supplies: Reserve for the OS, other processes and unaccounted growth
Admission points before large allocations and capacity increases
Denial handling: smaller chunks, fewer resident items or failing the request
Device memory checks through the device API
Disjoint incremental peak extents with already-charged bytes excluded; file-page estimates for CPU and upload paths
preserve: Unknown is never reported as zero
Dirty, writeback and shmem/tmpfs pages are not counted as reclaimable; malformed counters count nothing
Observations are snapshots; allocation failure remains authoritative
adapt: Reserve policy and acceptance of unknown observations
Additional sources such as job objects or container runtimes

code_files.purpose: Observations over any root (fixtures), Windows GlobalMemoryStatusEx and the admission rule

requires.hardware: Python 3.11+ standard library; native engines use Core's host_memory.h (crit::core)
requires.workload: Any engine making large host allocations on Linux or Windows; other platforms report unknown

contract.input: A filesystem root on Linux (default /), a request size and a reserve; Python working-set variant takes disjoint anonymous, pinned and additional clean file-page bytes
contract.output: Observation(physical, commit, cgroup, notes) and Decision(admitted, binding, limit, reason)
contract.ownership: Read-only; nothing is allocated, reserved or changed
contract.failure: Unreadable or absent sources yield unknown observations with notes; negative requests or reserves are rejected; with no known observation admission is denied unless explicitly allowed; working-set admission requires physical observation by default for nonzero incremental demand and rejects malformed extents
contract.core_boundary: Native observations and working-set admission are Core's (observe_host_memory, admit_host in crit/host_memory.h); this entry keeps the Python reference and admission guidance. Both complement Core's logical resource reservations with OS observations before allocation

validation.host: Synthetic /proc and /sys trees: enforced and unenforced commit, cgroup v2 ancestors with dirty, writeback and shmem pages, memory.high, cgroup v1, malformed counters and limits, missing sources, reserve and exact-fit admission, unknown policy, and a live observation; working-set tests independently bind RAM, commit and cgroup headroom, including unknown and zero-demand paths
validation.native: No native code here; Core's io fixture covers observe_host_memory_linux over synthetic trees (cgroup v1, nested and hybrid v2, shmem, memory.high, malformed values) with the same cases as the Python fixtures, admit_host and a live observation
validation.performance: No claim that an admitted allocation succeeds or avoids paging
